title: 计算机科学，从零搭建 · 第55部分：对信任的信任

chapters.Memory: 2. 内存破坏，以及面向返回的编程
chapters.Trojan: 11. 关于对信任的信任的反思
chapters.Frontier: 14. 前沿：这个系列的开放问题
chapters.Outro: 回顾、习题，以及它们会在哪里再出现

818edec4453d.en: This series built a tower, from gates to a cluster, and claimed at every level that the layer above need not care how the layer below works. <bookmark mark='a'/> Security is where that claim fails. Hammer one row of memory and bits flip in its neighbours. Speculate past a branch and a secret leaves a trace in the cache. Overflow a buffer and a function returns into the attacker's input. <bookmark mark='b'/> A kernel bug crosses a sandbox's wall; a compiler can insert a backdoor that no source shows; one BGP announcement steals a block of the internet; a string typed into a web form becomes code; and in 2024 a maintainer of a compression library hid a backdoor in it for two years. <bookmark mark='c'/> An attacker needs one weak layer. A defender must hold them all.
818edec4453d.zh: 这个系列搭了一座塔，从门电路一直搭到集群，并且在每一层都宣称：上面的一层不必关心下面的一层是怎么工作的。<bookmark mark='a'/>安全，正是这个说法失效的地方。反复敲打内存的一行，它邻居里的比特就会翻转。越过一个分支去推测执行，一个秘密就会在缓存里留下痕迹。让缓冲区溢出，一个函数就会返回到攻击者的输入里。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个内核漏洞可以越过沙箱的墙；编译器可以插入一个在任何源代码里都看不到的后门；一条 BGP 通告就能偷走互联网的一块地址；在网页表单里输入的一个字符串会变成代码；而在2024年，一个压缩库的维护者在里面藏了一个后门，藏了两年。<bookmark mark='c'/>攻击者只需要一个薄弱的层。防御者却必须守住所有的层。

e7291eccad3b.en: And then there is the attack that closes this series. <bookmark mark='a'/> In his Turing Award lecture of 1984 Ken Thompson described a compiler that inserts a backdoor whenever it compiles the login program, and inserts itself whenever it compiles a compiler. <bookmark mark='b'/> We built it. Here are the hashes of our clean compiler, of the trojaned one, <bookmark mark='c'/> and of a compiler rebuilt from the clean source by the trojaned binary. The last two are identical, byte for byte. <bookmark mark='d'/> Delete the trojan from every source file and it survives in the binary forever, still letting a secret password into login. By the end of this part we will catch it.
e7291eccad3b.zh: 然后是为这个系列收尾的那种攻击。<bookmark mark='a'/>在1984年的图灵奖演讲里，肯·汤普森描述了一个编译器：每当它编译 login 程序，就插入一个后门；每当它编译一个编译器，就把它自己插进去。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们把它造出来了。这里是我们干净的编译器的哈希，被植入木马的那个编译器的哈希，<bookmark mark='c'/>以及一个编译器的哈希，它是由被植入木马的二进制文件，用干净的源代码重新构建出来的。后两个一模一样，逐字节相同。<bookmark mark='d'/>把木马从每一个源文件里删掉，它仍然永远活在二进制文件里，仍然让一个秘密密码进入 login。到这一部分结束时，我们会抓住它。

d4c60b92b447.en: This is Part 55 of Computer Science, Built, the last part of the degree. <bookmark mark='a'/> We will set out threat models and the classic design principles; corrupt memory and chain gadgets without injecting code, then see what memory safety proves; follow leaks through hardware; authenticate, and find a famous protocol's flaw with a model checker; control access and isolate; break the web, the network and the supply chain; build Thompson's trojan and catch it; and finally walk the tower, from a NAND gate to a cluster, one last time.
d4c60b92b447.zh: 这是《计算机科学，从零搭建》的第55部分，也是这门学位课程的最后一部分。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们会先列出威胁模型和经典的设计原则；破坏内存，不注入代码就把 gadget 串成链，然后看内存安全证明了什么；顺着硬件追踪泄漏；做身份认证，并用模型检验器找出一个著名协议的缺陷；做访问控制与隔离；攻破 Web、网络和供应链；搭建肯·汤普森的特洛伊木马并抓住它；最后，从一个与非门到一个集群，把整座塔再走最后一遍。

d6fa29964f81.en: Chapter one. Threat models, and principles.
d6fa29964f81.zh: 第一章：威胁模型与原则。

10c69b65264c.en: Before any attack or defence, one question: what does it mean for a system to be secure? <bookmark mark='a'/> The classic answer is three promises. Confidentiality: only the people who should read something can read it. Integrity: only the people who should change it can change it. Availability: it is there when it is needed. <bookmark mark='b'/> A breach is any one of the three broken, and different systems weigh them differently. A bank fears a forged transfer more than a leak; a hospital may fear its records being gone more than being read. Security is never absolute; it is always security of something, against someone.
10c69b65264c.zh: 在讨论任何攻击或防御之前，先问一个问题：一个系统“安全”意味着什么？<bookmark mark='a'/>经典的回答是三个承诺。机密性：只有应该读它的人才能读。完整性：只有应该改它的人才能改。可用性：需要的时候它就在那里。<bookmark mark='b'/>三者只要有一个被破坏，系统就算被攻破了，而不同的系统对这三者的看重不同。银行更怕转账被伪造，而不是信息泄露；医院可能更怕记录丢失，而不是被人读到。安全从来不是绝对的；它永远是某个东西的安全，是针对某个人的安全。

07abbe4809f2.en: To defend a system you first describe the fight. That description is a threat model. <bookmark mark='a'/> It names the assets worth protecting: here, a login program, the files, the keys. <bookmark mark='b'/> It draws a trust boundary around the part that must be correct, the trusted computing base, and admits that everything inside it is trusted whether it deserves to be or not. <bookmark mark='c'/> It names the adversary and what they can do: can they send packets, run a program, sit on the same machine, bribe a maintainer? <bookmark mark='d'/> And it maps the attack surface, every way in. The danger is always what the model leaves out, because that is exactly where the attacker will look.
07abbe4809f2.zh: 要保卫一个系统，先要描述这场较量。这份描述就是威胁模型。<bookmark mark='a'/>它列出值得保护的资产：这里是一个登录程序、文件和密钥。<bookmark mark='b'/>它围绕那个必须正确的部分画出一条信任边界，那就是可信计算基，并承认其中的一切都是被信任的，不论它配不配得上。<bookmark mark='c'/>它指明对手以及对手能做什么：能不能发送数据包，运行一个程序，待在同一台机器上，贿赂一个维护者？<bookmark mark='d'/>它还描绘出攻击面，也就是每一条进入的途径。危险永远在于模型遗漏的东西，因为那恰恰是攻击者会去找的地方。

90bfb14629bc.en: This part is a tour of attacks, so here are the landmarks, with the dates this series is sure of. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1988 the Morris worm spread across the early internet, partly through a buffer overflow in a network service. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 1996 an article by the author who wrote as Aleph One explained the stack overflow carefully enough that anyone could follow it. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 2014 Rowhammer showed that software could flip bits in memory it never touched; in 2018 Spectre and Meltdown showed that speculation leaks secrets; and in 2024 a backdoor was found hidden in a widely used compression library. <bookmark mark='d'/> Four decades, and every layer of the tower we built.
90bfb14629bc.zh: 这一部分是一次攻击之旅，所以先列出路标，日期都是这个系列有把握的。<bookmark mark='a'/>1988年，莫里斯蠕虫在早期的互联网上传播，部分是靠一个网络服务里的缓冲区溢出。<bookmark mark='b'/>1996年，一位以 Aleph One 为笔名写作的作者发表了一篇文章，把栈溢出讲得足够仔细，任何人都能跟着做。<bookmark mark='c'/>2014年，行锤攻击表明，软件可以翻转它从未碰过的内存里的比特；2018年，Spectre 和 Meltdown 表明，推测执行会泄露秘密；2024年，人们发现一个被广泛使用的压缩库里藏着后门。<bookmark mark='d'/>四十年，涵盖了我们所搭的塔的每一层。

f9d9941376be.en: Fifty years ago Jerome Saltzer and Michael Schroeder distilled the whole subject into a handful of design principles, and they have barely aged. <bookmark mark='a'/> Keep the mechanism small enough to inspect. Deny by default, and grant access deliberately. Check every access, every time, with no fast path that skips the check. <bookmark mark='b'/> Do not rest security on keeping the design secret, an idea older than them, from Kerckhoffs in the nineteenth century: assume the enemy knows the system. Require more than one key for the most dangerous actions. <bookmark mark='c'/> Give each part only the privileges it needs; share as little machinery as possible between users; and, above all, make it usable, because a control people cannot live with is a control they will switch off. They listed two more: raise the attacker's work factor, and record compromises when you cannot prevent them.
f9d9941376be.zh: 五十年前，Jerome Saltzer 和 Michael Schroeder 把整个主题提炼成了几条设计原则，而这些原则几乎没有过时。<bookmark mark='a'/>让机制小到可以检查。默认拒绝，并有意识地授予访问权。每次访问都要检查，每一次都检查，不留任何跳过检查的捷径。<bookmark mark='b'/>不要把安全建立在设计保密之上，这个想法比他们更早，来自十九世纪的 Kerckhoffs：假设敌人了解这个系统。对最危险的操作，要求不止一把钥匙。<bookmark mark='c'/>只给每个部分它所需要的权限；用户之间尽可能少地共享机制；而最重要的是，要让它好用，因为人们无法忍受的控制措施，人们就会把它关掉。他们还列出了两条：提高攻击者的工作因子，以及在无法阻止被攻破时，把它记录下来。

eec52b448500.en: There is a deep asymmetry underneath all of this. <bookmark mark='a'/> The attacker needs to find one way in. The defender must hold every layer at once, from the hardware to the supply chain, and a single weak one is enough. <bookmark mark='b'/> That is why the practical answers are modest. Defence in depth: many imperfect walls, so that breaching one does not win the game. A trusted computing base kept as small as you can bear, because everything in it is a thing that must be right. And the working assumption of modern security, that you have already been breached, so you also plan to detect it and recover. The rest of this part walks the layers, one at a time, and shows each one leaking.
eec52b448500.zh: 这一切的底下，有一种深刻的不对称。<bookmark mark='a'/>攻击者只需要找到一条路进去。防御者必须同时守住每一层，从硬件到供应链，而只要有一层薄弱就够了。<bookmark mark='b'/>这就是为什么实用的回答都很朴素。纵深防御：许多道并不完美的墙，这样攻破一道并不等于赢下全局。把可信计算基保持得小到你能承受的程度，因为其中的每一样东西，都必须是对的。还有现代安全的工作假设：你已经被攻破了，所以你还要计划如何发现它并恢复。这一部分的其余内容，会一层一层地走过这些层，并展示每一层是怎样泄漏的。

ac42a2ea0c1d.en: Chapter two. Memory corruption, and return-oriented programming.
ac42a2ea0c1d.zh: 第二章：内存破坏，以及面向返回的编程。

dd06494a002c.en: We begin where Part 11 left a loose thread. A function keeps its local variables on the stack: here a sixty-four byte buffer, some saved registers, and, just above them, the address the function will return to. <bookmark mark='a'/> Now copy input into the buffer with a routine that has no bound. This is C's gets, so dangerous it was removed from the language in 2011. <bookmark mark='b'/> Give it more than sixty-four bytes and it writes straight past the buffer, over the saved registers, and over the saved return address. When the function returns, it jumps wherever those overwritten bytes point. <bookmark mark='c'/> Point it back into the buffer, which now holds the attacker's own instructions, and the program is theirs. This is the overflow the Morris worm used in 1988 and the article by Aleph One explained in 1996.
dd06494a002c.zh: 我们从第11部分留下一个线头的地方开始。一个函数把它的局部变量放在栈上：这里是一个64字节的缓冲区、一些保存的寄存器，以及就在它们上方、这个函数将要返回到的地址。<bookmark mark='a'/>现在用一个没有边界的例程把输入复制进缓冲区。这就是 C 语言的 gets，它危险到在2011年被从语言里删除了。<bookmark mark='b'/>给它超过64字节，它就会一路写过缓冲区，覆盖保存的寄存器，再覆盖保存的返回地址。函数返回时，它会跳到那些被覆盖的字节所指的任何地方。<bookmark mark='c'/>让它指回缓冲区，那里现在放着攻击者自己的指令，于是程序就归他们了。这就是1988年莫里斯蠕虫用过的、1996年 Aleph One 的文章讲解的那种溢出。

88dcacca115b.en: Three defences answered this attack, and we ran our Pebble overflow under every combination. <bookmark mark='a'/> A stack canary is a secret word just before the return address, checked on the way out; an overflow reaching the return address changes it first. <bookmark mark='b'/> W, xor, X means memory is writable or executable but never both, so the stack can hold the attacker's bytes but the processor refuses to run them. <bookmark mark='c'/> And address-space layout randomisation scatters the addresses, so the one the attacker wrote usually points nowhere. <bookmark mark='d'/> Look at the table: any one of the three turns a clean takeover into a crash or a caught attempt. The attacker now needs to beat all three.
88dcacca115b.zh: 有三种防御来应对这种攻击，我们让自己的 Pebble 溢出在每一种组合下都跑了一遍。<bookmark mark='a'/>栈金丝雀，是紧挨在返回地址之前的一个秘密的字，在退出时检查；溢出要碰到返回地址，会先改掉它。<bookmark mark='b'/>写异或执行，意思是内存可写或可执行，但绝不兼得，所以栈可以存放攻击者的字节，但处理器拒绝运行它们。<bookmark mark='c'/>地址空间布局随机化把地址打散，所以攻击者写下的那个地址，通常指向无处。<bookmark mark='d'/>看这张表：三者中的任何一个，都会把一次干净的接管变成一次崩溃，或者一次被抓住的尝试。现在攻击者需要同时击败这三者。

12f262b432c4.en: ASLR is a probability, not a wall, so let us do the arithmetic the way Part 27 would. <bookmark mark='a'/> With k random bits in an address there are two to the k equally likely placements, and a fixed exploit guesses one, so it succeeds with probability two to the minus k. <bookmark mark='b'/> If the layout is re-randomised on every attempt, the number of tries to the first hit is a geometric random variable with mean one over p, which is two to the k. <bookmark mark='c'/> Here are the published entropies for typical layouts: a thirty-two bit system gives only sixteen bits on one base, brute-forced in about sixty-five thousand tries, which Shacham and colleagues did in 2004; a sixty-four bit system gives nearer thirty. <bookmark mark='d'/> And a small runnable version on Pebble confirms the formula exactly: of sixty-four placements, one matches, a rate of one in sixty-four.
12f262b432c4.zh: ASLR 是一种概率，而不是一堵墙，所以我们像第27部分那样来算一算。<bookmark mark='a'/>地址里有 k 个随机比特，就有 2 的 k 次方种等可能的放置方式，而一个固定的攻击只猜其中一种，所以它成功的概率是 2 的负 k 次方。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果每次尝试布局都重新随机化，那么到第一次命中所需的尝试次数，就是一个几何随机变量，均值是 p 分之一，也就是 2 的 k 次方。<bookmark mark='c'/>这是已发表的典型布局的熵：32位系统在一个基址上只有16比特，大约试65000次就能暴力破解，Shacham 和同事在2004年就做到了；64位系统则接近30比特。<bookmark mark='d'/>在 Pebble 上，一个可以运行的小版本精确地印证了这个公式：64种放置方式里，有一种匹配，比率是64分之1。

3f6a56742231.en: W, xor, X stops injected code. In 2007 Hovav Shacham showed it does not stop the attacker. <bookmark mark='a'/> Instead of new code, reuse code already there: short instruction sequences that end in a return, called gadgets. <bookmark mark='b'/> The overflow now writes a train of return addresses on the stack. Each return jumps to a gadget, which does a little work and returns into the next. <bookmark mark='c'/> Our Pebble binary has eight gadgets, and a chain of them makes the program print its word and halt with W, xor, X fully on. No stack code ever ran. <bookmark mark='d'/> The canary still trips first, which is why real chains also need a leak. The lesson: control flow is the asset to defend.
3f6a56742231.zh: 写异或执行能挡住被注入的代码。2007年，Hovav Shacham 表明，它挡不住攻击者。<bookmark mark='a'/>不用新代码，而是重用已经在那里的代码：以返回指令结尾的短指令序列，称为 gadget。<bookmark mark='b'/>溢出现在往栈上写下一串返回地址。每一次返回都跳到一个 gadget，它做一点工作，再返回到下一个。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们的 Pebble 二进制文件里有8个 gadget，用其中的一条链，就能让程序在写异或执行完全开启的情况下，打印出它的词并停机。栈上的代码一行也没有运行过。<bookmark mark='d'/>金丝雀仍然会最先被触发，这就是为什么真实的攻击链还需要一次泄漏。教训是：控制流是要保卫的资产。

8358a146981b.en: So defend control flow directly. <bookmark mark='a'/> Control-flow integrity, from Martin Abadi and colleagues in 2005, checks at each indirect jump or return that the target is one the compiler allowed; a chain that lands mid-gadget fails. <bookmark mark='b'/> A shadow stack keeps a protected copy of every return address, now in hardware. <bookmark mark='c'/> CHERI makes each pointer a capability carrying its bounds, so a forged pointer cannot be built. <bookmark mark='d'/> Each raises the cost; none ends the war. Could the language make the bug impossible?
8358a146981b.zh: 那就直接保卫控制流。<bookmark mark='a'/>控制流完整性，由 Martin Abadi 和同事在2005年提出，在每一次间接跳转或返回时，检查目标是不是编译器允许的那一个；落在 gadget 中间的链会失败。<bookmark mark='b'/>影子栈为每个返回地址保留一份受保护的副本，如今已经做进了硬件。<bookmark mark='c'/>CHERI 让每个指针成为一个携带着自己边界的能力（capability），所以伪造的指针造不出来。<bookmark mark='d'/>每一种都抬高了代价；没有一种能终结这场战争。能不能让语言本身使这个错误不可能发生？

d8b40ebacea0.en: Canaries, W, xor, X and control-flow integrity all fight the overflow after it is written. The question of this chapter is whether we can stop writing it at all, and the reason the question matters is a single number. <bookmark mark='a'/> Around 2019 both Microsoft and the Chromium project reported the same thing: roughly seventy per cent of their serious security bugs were memory-safety bugs. <bookmark mark='b'/> Buffer overflows, use-after-free, double frees, reads past the end of an array, uninitialised memory. Not clever cryptographic breaks, but the same handful of mistakes, made over and over, in languages that let you make them. <bookmark mark='c'/> If a language could forbid that whole category, it would remove most of the vulnerabilities people actually ship.
d8b40ebacea0.zh: 金丝雀、写异或执行和控制流完整性，都是在溢出被写出来之后才去对付它。这一章的问题是：我们能不能干脆不再写出它。这个问题之所以重要，原因是一个数字。<bookmark mark='a'/>2019年前后，Microsoft 和 Chromium 项目报告了同一件事：它们严重的安全漏洞里，大约70%是内存安全漏洞。<bookmark mark='b'/>缓冲区溢出，释放后使用，重复释放，读过数组末尾，未初始化的内存。不是什么巧妙的密码学攻破，而是同样的那几种错误，在允许人们犯这些错误的语言里，一遍又一遍地被犯下。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果一门语言能禁止这整个类别，它就能消除人们实际发布出去的大部分漏洞。

174ed64cc17e.en: Rust's answer reaches back to Part 14 and the typed lambda calculus. <bookmark mark='a'/> In an ordinary type system there is a rule called contraction: if a variable is in scope you may use it as many times as you wish. <bookmark mark='b'/> Drop that rule and you get an affine type, where a value may be used at most once. Rust builds its whole discipline on this: every value has exactly one owner, and assigning it to someone else moves it, so the old name is no longer usable. <bookmark mark='c'/> You can lend a value out instead of moving it. A shared borrow gives many readers and no writer; a unique mutable borrow gives one writer and no one else. Every borrow ends, returning the value to its owner; but a move is final, and using what you moved is a compile error, not a crash.
174ed64cc17e.zh: Rust 的回答要追溯到第14部分和带类型的 λ 演算。<bookmark mark='a'/>在普通的类型系统里，有一条叫作收缩的规则：只要一个变量在作用域内，你想用多少次就能用多少次。<bookmark mark='b'/>去掉这条规则，就得到仿射类型，其中一个值最多只能用一次。Rust 的整套规矩都建立在这上面：每个值恰好有一个所有者，把它赋给别人就是移动它，于是旧的名字不能再用了。<bookmark mark='c'/>你可以把一个值借出去，而不是移动它。共享借用给出许多读者而没有写者；独占的可变借用给出一个写者，其他人都不行。每一次借用都会结束，把值还给它的所有者；但移动是最终的，使用你已经移动走的东西，是编译错误，而不是崩溃。

95ffed64bc97.en: To see what the rule buys, we built a toy borrow checker and ran it on ten small programs. <bookmark mark='a'/> It enforces four things, each the cause of a real class of bug. No use after a move, which would be a dangling reference. No two mutable borrows at once, which would be a data race. No shared and mutable borrow together, so no one reads a value while another is changing it. And no reference outliving the value it points at, which is use-after-free by another name. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each rejected program is rejected with a reason, at compile time, and each sound one is accepted; moving a value and then using the destination is fine, lending it within its lifetime is fine. <bookmark mark='c'/> This is the borrow checker in miniature: it turns the whole seventy per cent into errors the compiler catches before the program ever runs.
95ffed64bc97.zh: 为了看看这条规则换来了什么，我们搭了一个玩具借用检查器，在10个小程序上运行它。<bookmark mark='a'/>它强制执行四件事，每一件都是一类真实错误的成因。移动之后不得使用，否则就是悬空引用。不得同时有两个可变借用，否则就是数据竞争。共享借用和可变借用不得同时存在，所以没有人在另一个人修改一个值的时候去读它。引用不得比它所指向的值活得更久，那就是换了个名字的释放后使用。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个被拒绝的程序，都是带着理由、在编译时被拒绝的，而每个合理的程序都被接受；移动一个值然后使用目的地，没问题，在它的生命周期内借出去，也没问题。<bookmark mark='c'/>这就是微缩版的借用检查器：它把那整整70%变成了编译器在程序运行之前就能抓住的错误。

9542544b65c9.en: What exactly has been proved? <bookmark mark='a'/> A program the borrow checker accepts has, by construction, no use-after-free, no double free, no data race and no dangling pointer. The absence is guaranteed, not merely tested. <bookmark mark='b'/> But some things genuinely need raw pointers, so Rust keeps an escape hatch, marked unsafe, and you use it to build the safe data structures everyone else relies on. The danger is not removed; it is penned into small blocks a human can audit. <bookmark mark='c'/> And here the series closes a loop. In 2018 the RustBelt project gave a machine-checked proof that the type system stays sound even accounting for that unsafe code inside the standard library, exactly the Part 54 idea of shrinking the trusted base and then verifying it. <bookmark mark='d'/> It is not a cure-all. Logic errors remain, the unsafe core must still be right, and the world's existing C and C plus plus will not rewrite itself, which is a problem we leave for the frontier.
9542544b65c9.zh: 到底证明了什么？<bookmark mark='a'/>借用检查器接受的程序，从构造上就没有释放后使用，没有重复释放，没有数据竞争，也没有悬空指针。这种不存在是有保证的，而不只是测试过的。<bookmark mark='b'/>但有些事情确实需要裸指针，所以 Rust 保留了一个逃生口，标记为 unsafe，你用它来构建所有其他人所依赖的安全数据结构。危险并没有被消除；它被圈进了一些小块里，人可以对它们逐一审查。<bookmark mark='c'/>而在这里，这个系列把一个圈合上了。2018年，RustBelt 项目给出了一个机器检查的证明：即使把标准库里的那些 unsafe 代码计算在内，这个类型系统依然是可靠的，这正是第54部分的想法：缩小可信的基础，然后验证它。<bookmark mark='d'/>它不是万灵药。逻辑错误依然存在，unsafe 的核心仍然必须是对的，而世界上现有的 C 和 C++ 不会自己重写，这个问题我们留给前沿。

3df5f13fd859.en: Chapter four. When the hardware leaks.

08f595f23263.en: Start at the bottom of the tower, with the memory itself, and recall Part 5. <bookmark mark='a'/> Pick two rows of DRAM and open them alternately, over and over, as fast as the machine allows. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each activation disturbs the row physically between them and drains a little charge from its cells, cells a program is never touching at all. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 2014 Yoongu Kim and colleagues measured this: of a hundred and twenty-nine DDR3 modules, a hundred and ten flipped bits, some after only about a hundred and thirty-nine thousand activations, well inside one sixty-four millisecond refresh period. A reliability margin had quietly become a security boundary. <bookmark mark='d'/> The defences, refreshing more often, counting activations, error-correcting codes, each helped and each was later worked around: in 2020 new access patterns flipped bits on DDR4 that had them all.
08f595f23263.zh: 从塔的最底层开始，从内存本身开始，回想第5部分。<bookmark mark='a'/>选两行 DRAM，轮流打开它们，一遍又一遍，以机器允许的最快速度。<bookmark mark='b'/>每一次激活，都会在物理上干扰它们之间的那一行，从它的单元里漏走一点电荷，而这些单元，程序根本从来没有碰过。<bookmark mark='c'/>2014年，Yoongu Kim 和同事测量了这一点：在129条 DDR3 内存条里，有110条出现了比特翻转，有些只需要大约139000次激活，远远落在一个64毫秒的刷新周期之内。一个可靠性的余量，悄悄变成了安全的边界。<bookmark mark='d'/>这些防御，更频繁地刷新、对激活计数、纠错码，每一种都有帮助，也每一种后来都被绕过了：2020年，新的访问模式在配备了所有这些措施的 DDR4 上翻转了比特。

3976ecd2088c.en: Now climb one layer, to the processor, and recall Part 8. <bookmark mark='a'/> To stay fast, the core guesses which way a branch will go and runs ahead before the guess is checked. Here it guesses that an index is in bounds and speculatively reads past the end of an array, then uses that secret byte to touch one line of a probe array. <bookmark mark='b'/> When the guess turns out wrong, the processor rolls the work back: architecturally, those instructions never happened. But the cache line it touched is still warm, and that it cannot undo. <bookmark mark='c'/> So the attacker times a read of every line; the one that is fast names the secret byte. That timing trick is Flush and Reload, from Yarom and Falkner in 2014, and it is how Spectre and Meltdown, disclosed in 2018, read memory across a boundary that every bounds check and every privilege bit said was closed.
3976ecd2088c.zh: 现在往上爬一层，到处理器，回想第8部分。<bookmark mark='a'/>为了保持快速，核心会猜一个分支往哪边走，并在猜测被检验之前就往前跑。这里它猜一个下标在界内，于是推测地读过了数组的末尾，然后用那个秘密字节去触碰探测数组的一行。<bookmark mark='b'/>当猜测被证明是错的，处理器会把这些工作回滚：在体系结构层面，那些指令从未发生过。但它所触碰的那条缓存行依然是热的，这一点它无法撤销。<bookmark mark='c'/>于是攻击者给每一行的读取计时；快的那一行，就指明了那个秘密字节。这个计时的技巧是 Flush and Reload，由 Yarom 和 Falkner 在2014年提出，而2018年披露的 Spectre 和 Meltdown，正是靠它读到了跨越边界的内存，而每一次边界检查、每一个特权位都说这条边界是关闭的。

e3effef3e099.en: Rowhammer and Spectre are two cases of a wider truth, the one Parts 8 and 29 kept meeting. <bookmark mark='a'/> A computation says more than its output. It leaks through how long it takes, how much power it draws, what it leaves in the cache, even the sound the capacitors make. <bookmark mark='b'/> The classic example is a comparison that stops at the first wrong byte. The more of a guess is right, the longer it runs, so the time quietly tells the attacker how close they are, and they recover a secret one byte at a time. Paul Kocher showed in 1996 that timing alone breaks real cryptography. <bookmark mark='c'/> The defence is to write code whose running time and memory use do not depend on the secret at all, so the line is flat. It is called constant-time code, and it is as much a discipline as a technique.
e3effef3e099.zh: 行锤攻击和 Spectre 是一个更宽泛的真相的两个例子，也是第8部分和第29部分一再遇到的那个真相。<bookmark mark='a'/>一次计算说出的，比它的输出更多。它通过自己花多长时间、耗多少电力、在缓存里留下什么，甚至电容发出的声音，泄露信息。<bookmark mark='b'/>经典的例子是一个遇到第一个错误字节就停下的比较。猜测对的部分越多，它运行得越久，于是时间悄悄告诉攻击者他们有多接近，他们就一次一个字节地恢复出一个秘密。Paul Kocher 在1996年表明，单靠计时就能攻破真实的密码学。<bookmark mark='c'/>防御的办法，是写出这样的代码：它的运行时间和内存使用完全不依赖于那个秘密，于是那条线是平的。这叫作恒定时间代码，它既是一种技术，也同样是一种纪律。

8989c5adeecb.en: Step back, because these share one shape, and it is the thread of the whole series. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every layer makes a promise so the layer above need not look down. Memory holds what you wrote. Rolled-back work leaves no trace. The answer is all you learn. <bookmark mark='b'/> A side channel is the physics underneath, the charge, the timing, the shared cache, showing through the promise. <bookmark mark='c'/> And the fixes are never free: a speculation barrier or a faster refresh costs real performance, so the roofline of Part 9 moves the wrong way. <bookmark mark='d'/> The direction the field has taken is to stop pretending, and to write down a contract between hardware and software that states exactly what the layer below promises not to leak, so the layer above can finally rely on it.
8989c5adeecb.zh: 退后一步，因为这些情形有着同一个形状，它就是整个系列的主线。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一层都做出一个承诺，好让上面的一层不必往下看。内存保存你写进去的东西。被回滚的工作不留痕迹。你得到的只有答案。<bookmark mark='b'/>侧信道，就是底下的物理，电荷、时间、共享的缓存，透过这个承诺显露出来。<bookmark mark='c'/>而且修复从来不是免费的：一道推测屏障或者更快的刷新，要付出真实的性能代价，所以第9部分的屋顶线朝错误的方向移动了。<bookmark mark='d'/>这个领域所选择的方向，是不再假装，并把硬件和软件之间的一份契约写下来，准确说明下面一层承诺不泄漏什么，好让上面一层终于可以依赖它。

848d5bcf6bec.en: Chapter five. Who are you? Authentication.
848d5bcf6bec.zh: 第五章：你是谁？身份认证。

7023827803a5.en: Start with the oldest answer: something you know. <bookmark mark='a'/> A password of L symbols, each from an alphabet of N, is one of N to the L. <bookmark mark='b'/> Its entropy in bits is the base-two logarithm of that count, <bookmark mark='c'/> which is L times log two of N. <bookmark mark='d'/> Testing R guesses a second, an attacker expects to search half the space: two to the H over two R. <bookmark mark='e'/> At ten billion guesses a second, a fast hash on one graphics card, eight lowercase letters last about ten seconds; sixteen last some seventy thousand years.
7023827803a5.zh: 从最古老的回答开始：你知道的东西。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个由 L 个符号组成的密码，每个符号取自 N 个字符的字母表，它是 N 的 L 次方种可能中的一种。<bookmark mark='b'/>它以比特计的熵，是这个数目以2为底的对数，<bookmark mark='c'/>也就是 L 乘以 N 的以2为底的对数。<bookmark mark='d'/>每秒测试 R 次猜测，攻击者预期要搜索一半的空间：2 的 H 次方除以 2R。<bookmark mark='e'/>以每秒100亿次猜测计，这是一块显卡上的快速哈希，8个小写字母只能撑大约10秒；16个能撑大约7万年。

ee07f8ebb070.en: But entropy assumes a random choice, and people do not choose at random. <bookmark mark='a'/> Large studies, Joseph Bonneau's in 2012 among them, found choices close to a Zipf law: the r-th most popular password is chosen with probability proportional to one over r. <bookmark mark='b'/> In our illustrative model of ten million passwords, ten guesses cover eighteen percent of users, and a million cover eighty-six. <bookmark mark='c'/> The share is a ratio of harmonic numbers, and a harmonic number is a logarithm, <bookmark mark='d'/> so every tenfold increase in guesses adds the same slice, about fourteen points.
ee07f8ebb070.zh: 但熵假设的是随机选择，而人们并不随机选择。<bookmark mark='a'/>大型研究，包括 Joseph Bonneau 在2012年的那一项，发现人们的选择接近齐普夫定律：第 r 流行的密码，被选中的概率与 r 分之一成正比。<bookmark mark='b'/>在我们这个有1000万个密码的示意模型里，猜10次就覆盖18%的用户，猜100万次覆盖86%。<bookmark mark='c'/>这个占比是调和数的比值，而调和数就是一个对数，<bookmark mark='d'/>所以每把猜测次数增加到10倍，就加上同样大的一块，大约14个百分点。

78f5dccc6f58.en: Assume the password file will be stolen, and make the theft buy little. <bookmark mark='a'/> Store only a hash. Unsalted, equal passwords give equal hashes, and one precomputed table cracks them all. <bookmark mark='b'/> A random salt per user makes every entry different, so each user must be attacked alone. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then make the hash slow on purpose: time is inversely proportional to rate, <bookmark mark='d'/> so going from ten billion guesses a second to ten is a factor of a billion: eight lowercase letters now take over three hundred years per core. <bookmark mark='e'/> These are Part 29's bcrypt, scrypt and Argon2, the last two also demanding memory.
78f5dccc6f58.zh: 假设密码文件会被偷走，并让这次偷窃换不来多少东西。<bookmark mark='a'/>只存哈希。不加盐的话，相同的密码给出相同的哈希，一张预先算好的表就能把它们全部破解。<bookmark mark='b'/>给每个用户一个随机的盐，让每一项都不同，于是每个用户都必须单独攻击。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后有意把哈希做慢：时间与速率成反比，<bookmark mark='d'/>所以从每秒100亿次猜测降到每秒10次，是10亿倍的差距：8个小写字母现在每个核心要超过300年。<bookmark mark='e'/>这就是第29部分的 bcrypt、scrypt 和 Argon2，后两者还要求用内存。

e255116a1981.en: A second factor proves something you have. <bookmark mark='a'/> Authenticator codes follow RFC 6238, from 2011. Phone and server share a key, and each divides the time by thirty seconds, rounding down, to get a counter. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each takes an HMAC of the counter, cuts four bytes from it where the hash itself points, and keeps the last six or eight digits. <bookmark mark='c'/> Ours reproduces the standard's test values exactly. <bookmark mark='d'/> At fifty-nine seconds the counter is one, and the code ends in the same six digits as the older counter-based code at counter one: the same computation. <bookmark mark='e'/> But it is still typed, so a fake page can relay it.
e255116a1981.zh: 第二因素证明的是你拥有的东西。<bookmark mark='a'/>验证器应用的验证码遵循 RFC 6238，发布于2011年。手机和服务器共享一把密钥，各自把时间除以30秒并向下取整，得到一个计数器。<bookmark mark='b'/>各自对这个计数器取一个 HMAC，在哈希自己所指的位置截取4个字节，并保留最后6位或8位数字。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们的实现精确地复现了标准里的测试值。<bookmark mark='d'/>在59秒时计数器是1，验证码末尾的6位数字，和较早的基于计数器的验证码在计数器为1时的一样：是同一种计算。<bookmark mark='e'/>但它仍然是要键入的，所以假页面可以把它转发出去。

67a260ca707d.en: Passkeys drop the shared secret, using Part 30's signatures. <bookmark mark='a'/> At sign-up the device makes a key pair for this one site and gives the server only the public half. <bookmark mark='b'/> To log in, the server sends a random challenge, the browser adds the origin it is really talking to, and the device signs both. <bookmark mark='c'/> The server checks the signature. Nothing secret is typed, and a stolen database logs no one in. <bookmark mark='d'/> A look-alike site gets a signature over the wrong origin, or none. This is WebAuthn, a W3C Recommendation since 2019.
67a260ca707d.zh: 通行密钥（passkey）抛开了共享的秘密，用的是第30部分的签名。<bookmark mark='a'/>注册时，设备为这一个网站生成一对密钥，只把公钥那一半交给服务器。<bookmark mark='b'/>登录时，服务器发来一个随机的挑战，浏览器加上它真正在与之通信的源，设备对两者一起签名。<bookmark mark='c'/>服务器检查签名。没有任何秘密需要键入，被偷走的数据库也登录不了任何人。<bookmark mark='d'/>一个外观相似的网站，只能得到一个对错误的源的签名，或者什么也得不到。这就是 WebAuthn，自2019年起是 W3C 推荐标准。

bb5b19274827.en: Across a network, logging in is a protocol. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1978 Roger Needham and Michael Schroeder proposed this one: Alice sends Bob a nonce and her name, sealed for Bob; he returns her nonce with one of his own; she returns his. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 1995 Gavin Lowe ran it through a model checker. Alice opens an honest session with the intruder, who re-seals her message for Bob. Bob's reply is sealed for Alice, so the intruder forwards it unread, and Alice returns Bob's nonce, to the intruder. <bookmark mark='c'/> Bob believes he is talking to Alice, and the intruder holds his secret. <bookmark mark='d'/> Our checker from Part 54 finds the same attack among nineteen states. <bookmark mark='e'/> Lowe's fix is a single name: Bob puts his own in the reply, and no attack remains.
bb5b19274827.zh: 跨越网络登录，是一个协议。<bookmark mark='a'/>1978年，Roger Needham 和 Michael Schroeder 提出了这一个：Alice 把一个一次性随机数（nonce）和她的名字，封装给 Bob 发过去；他把她的随机数连同他自己的一个返回；她再把他的那个返回。<bookmark mark='b'/>1995年，Gavin Lowe 把它放进模型检验器里跑了一遍。Alice 与入侵者开启了一次诚实的会话，入侵者把她的消息重新为 Bob 封装。Bob 的回复是为 Alice 封装的，所以入侵者原样转发而不读它，于是 Alice 把 Bob 的随机数返回给了入侵者。<bookmark mark='c'/>Bob 相信他在和 Alice 说话，而入侵者握有了他的秘密。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们第54部分的检验器，在19个状态之中找到了同样的攻击。<bookmark mark='e'/>Lowe 的修复只是一个名字：Bob 把他自己的名字放进回复里，攻击就不再存在。

d399900bad92.en: Authentication says who you are; access control decides what you may then do. <bookmark mark='a'/> Butler Lampson's paper Protection, in 1971, gave the field its picture: a matrix, with subjects such as users and processes down the side, objects such as files across the top, and in each cell the rights one holds over the other. <bookmark mark='b'/> A reference monitor consults it on every access. <bookmark mark='c'/> But real systems have millions of subjects and objects, with almost every cell empty, so no one stores the matrix whole.
d399900bad92.zh: 身份认证说明你是谁；访问控制则决定你随后可以做什么。<bookmark mark='a'/>Butler Lampson 1971年的论文《保护》（Protection），给了这个领域它的图景：一个矩阵，侧边是主体，比如用户和进程，顶端是客体，比如文件，每个格子里是一方对另一方持有的权限。<bookmark mark='b'/>引用监视器在每一次访问时都查询它。<bookmark mark='c'/>但真实的系统有几百万个主体和客体，几乎每个格子都是空的，所以没有人把矩阵完整地存起来。

d60fcca4ed5f.en: So systems store it in slices, and there are two ways to cut. <bookmark mark='a'/> Down a column, kept with the object: an access-control list, everyone who may touch this file, and how. Unix permission bits are a compressed one. <bookmark mark='b'/> Along a row, held by the subject: a list of capabilities, unforgeable tokens that both name an object and carry a right to it, like a file descriptor, which after the open is checked by possession alone. <bookmark mark='c'/> With lists on objects, revoking is easy; with tokens in hand, delegating is easy, and so is avoiding a classic mistake.
d60fcca4ed5f.zh: 所以系统是把它切成片来存的，有两种切法。<bookmark mark='a'/>沿着一列切，随对象保存：访问控制列表，也就是谁可以碰这个文件，以及怎样碰。Unix 的权限位就是一种压缩过的访问控制列表。<bookmark mark='b'/>沿着一行切，由主体持有：一张能力（capability）的列表，能力是不可伪造的令牌，既指明一个对象，又带着对它的一项权利，就像文件描述符那样，打开之后，只靠是否持有来检查。<bookmark mark='c'/>列表放在对象上，撤销就容易；令牌握在手里，委托就容易，避免一个经典的错误也容易。

ac73f7644392.en: Norm Hardy described that mistake in 1988, and called it the confused deputy. <bookmark mark='a'/> A compiler service may write two files of its own, a billing log and its debug output, and a client names the file for the debug output. <bookmark mark='b'/> With ambient authority the service writes with its own rights, whatever name it is given, so a client who names the billing file has it overwritten, with an authority the client never held. Our run does exactly that. <bookmark mark='c'/> With capabilities, the client must hand over a token for the output file, and it holds one only for its debug file, so the write is refused. <bookmark mark='d'/> Naming a thing and holding the right to it become one act.
ac73f7644392.zh: Norm Hardy 在1988年描述了那个错误，并把它叫作混淆代理（confused deputy）。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个编译器服务可以写它自己的两个文件，一个计费日志和它的调试输出，而客户端指定调试输出所用的文件。<bookmark mark='b'/>在环境权限（ambient authority）之下，服务用自己的权限来写，不管给它的是什么名字，所以指定了计费文件的客户端，会让它被覆盖，凭的是客户端从未拥有过的权限。我们的运行恰好就是这样。<bookmark mark='c'/>有了能力，客户端就必须交出输出文件的令牌，而它只持有调试文件的令牌，所以这次写入被拒绝。<bookmark mark='d'/>指名一个东西，和持有对它的权利，变成了同一个动作。

6d77d27e2f65.en: Sometimes the rule is about secrecy, not ownership. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1973 David Bell and Leonard LaPadula formalised military classification: every subject and object carries a label, a level and a set of categories. <bookmark mark='b'/> A subject may read only what its label dominates: no read up. <bookmark mark='c'/> And it may write only to what dominates it: no write down, so a secret process cannot copy into an unclassified file. <bookmark mark='d'/> Chain the two, and whatever a subject copies from one object to another moves up, never down. <bookmark mark='e'/> Our checks agree, including one flow that climbs a level and is still refused, for lack of a category. Biba's model of 1977 is the mirror image, for integrity.
6d77d27e2f65.zh: 有时规则关乎保密，而不是所有权。<bookmark mark='a'/>1973年，David Bell 和 Leonard LaPadula 把军事密级形式化了：每个主体和客体都带有一个标签，包括一个级别和一组类别。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个主体只能读它的标签所支配的东西：不得上读。<bookmark mark='c'/>而它只能写入标签支配自己的对象：不得下写，所以一个秘密的进程不能复制进一个未分级的文件。<bookmark mark='d'/>把两条串起来，一个主体从一个对象复制到另一个对象的任何东西，都只会往上走，绝不往下。<bookmark mark='e'/>我们的检查结果与此一致，包括一条升了一级却依然被拒绝的流动，原因是缺少一个类别。Biba 1977年的模型是它的镜像，针对的是完整性。

6bcaec5eedbb.en: Protection states also change, as owners grant rights. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1976 Harrison, Ruzzo and Ullman modelled a system as commands, each a test on the matrix followed by primitive edits. Here an owner may grant read, and may grant ownership itself. <bookmark mark='b'/> Is it safe? Can any sequence of commands put read into a cell that lacked it? <bookmark mark='c'/> Our breadth-first search finds a leak at once: Alice grants Eve read. <bookmark mark='d'/> A system whose only command revokes is safe. But our search is bounded, so safe means safe within its budget.
6bcaec5eedbb.zh: 保护状态也会改变，因为所有者会授予权限。<bookmark mark='a'/>1976年，Harrison、Ruzzo 和 Ullman 把一个系统建模成一组命令，每条命令是对矩阵的一次测试，后面跟着若干基本的修改。这里，所有者可以授予读权限，也可以授予所有权本身。<bookmark mark='b'/>它安全吗？有没有哪一串命令，能把读权限放进一个原本没有它的格子里？<bookmark mark='c'/>我们的广度优先搜索立刻就发现了一处泄漏：Alice 授予 Eve 读权限。<bookmark mark='d'/>一个唯一的命令是撤销的系统，是安全的。但我们的搜索是有界的，所以“安全”指的是在预算之内安全。

f43bdb5fcac5.en: Could a better search always answer? No, and the reason is Part 25. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take any Turing machine. Make each tape cell a subject, write its symbol, and the state where the head stands, on the diagonal, and let each cell own the next: the matrix is the tape. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each rule of the machine becomes a command. <bookmark mark='c'/> The halting state's right appears exactly when the machine halts, so deciding safety would decide halting. <bookmark mark='d'/> Safety is decidable only for restricted systems, such as those whose commands each make a single change: a strong argument for simple protection rules.
f43bdb5fcac5.zh: 更好的搜索能不能总是给出答案？不能，原因在第25部分。<bookmark mark='a'/>取任意一台图灵机。把每个纸带格子做成一个主体，把它的符号，以及读写头所在之处的状态，写在对角线上，并让每个格子拥有下一个格子：矩阵就是纸带。<bookmark mark='b'/>机器的每条规则变成一条命令。<bookmark mark='c'/>停机状态的那项权限，恰好在机器停机时出现，所以判定安全性，就等于判定停机。<bookmark mark='d'/>只有对受限的系统，安全性才是可判定的，比如那些每条命令只做一处修改的系统：这是支持采用简单保护规则的一个有力理由。

b66239b19df0.en: The first wall between programs is one we built in Parts 31 and 32. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every process has a page table, and can name only the memory its table maps. <bookmark mark='b'/> Two processes use the same address, page one, and reach different frames, each unaware of the other. <bookmark mark='c'/> Touch a page that is unmapped, or kept for the kernel, and the hardware traps to the kernel. Only the kernel may change a page table, because only it runs with the mode bit set. <bookmark mark='d'/> So the wall is exactly as strong as the kernel, and every one of its tens of millions of lines is trusted. <bookmark mark='e'/> The seL4 kernel, about ten thousand lines, is proved to enforce its isolation.
b66239b19df0.zh: 程序之间的第一堵墙，是我们在第31和32部分搭起来的。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个进程都有一张页表，并且只能指称它的页表所映射的内存。<bookmark mark='b'/>两个进程使用同一个地址，第1页，却到达了不同的页框，彼此毫不知情。<bookmark mark='c'/>触碰一个没有映射的页，或者一个留给内核的页，硬件就会陷入内核。只有内核可以修改页表，因为只有它是在模式位被设置的情况下运行的。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以这堵墙恰好和内核一样强，而它那几千万行代码中的每一行，都是被信任的。<bookmark mark='e'/>seL4 内核大约有一万行，已被证明会强制执行它的隔离。

5de740185e01.en: Processes are one rung on a ladder of walls. <bookmark mark='a'/> A language sandbox runs several programs inside one process. Processes share a kernel. Containers are processes given their own view of files and names, still on one kernel. Virtual machines each bring a kernel and share a hypervisor. Separate machines share only the network. <bookmark mark='b'/> Moving right, less is shared and the wall is stronger, but each rung costs more to run and to start. <bookmark mark='c'/> And an escape goes through whatever is shared: any kernel bug, such as the copy-on-write race called Dirty COW in 2016, is a possible container escape. <bookmark mark='d'/> In 2015 a bug called VENOM, in an emulated floppy-disk controller, let a virtual machine attack its host.
5de740185e01.zh: 进程只是墙的阶梯上的一级。<bookmark mark='a'/>语言沙箱在一个进程里运行好几个程序。进程共享一个内核。容器是被赋予了自己对文件和名字的视图的进程，仍然在同一个内核上。虚拟机各自带着一个内核，共享一个虚拟机管理程序。独立的机器只共享网络。<bookmark mark='b'/>往右走，共享的东西越来越少，墙越来越强，但每一级运行和启动的代价都更高。<bookmark mark='c'/>而逃逸会穿过任何被共享的东西：任何内核漏洞，比如2016年那个叫 Dirty COW 的写时复制竞争，都可能是一次容器逃逸。<bookmark mark='d'/>2015年，一个叫 VENOM 的漏洞，出在一个被模拟的软盘控制器里，让一台虚拟机攻击了它的宿主机。

2c5d0c9cf594.en: A process can also shrink its own power. <bookmark mark='a'/> A browser's renderer parses hostile pages, so once started it installs a filter on its own system calls. <bookmark mark='b'/> Calls on the allow-list, like read, write and exit, pass. Opening files, starting programs and making sockets are refused, so even a renderer the attacker fully controls can do little but compute. <bookmark mark='c'/> It is least privilege made mechanical: Linux has offered it since 2005 as seccomp, with filters written as small BPF programs since 2012. <bookmark mark='d'/> FreeBSD's Capsicum, from 2010, goes further: after one call a process loses every global name and keeps only the descriptors it holds, the capabilities of the last chapter.
2c5d0c9cf594.zh: 一个进程也可以缩小自己的权力。<bookmark mark='a'/>浏览器的渲染器要解析恶意的页面，所以它一启动，就给自己的系统调用装上一个过滤器。<bookmark mark='b'/>白名单上的调用，比如 read、write 和 exit，可以通过。打开文件、启动程序和创建套接字则被拒绝，所以即使是被攻击者完全控制的渲染器，也几乎只能做计算。<bookmark mark='c'/>这就是被机械化的最小权限：Linux 自2005年起就以 seccomp 的形式提供它，自2012年起，过滤器是以小型 BPF 程序的形式来写的。<bookmark mark='d'/>FreeBSD 在2010年的 Capsicum 走得更远：调用一次之后，进程就丢掉每一个全局名字，只保留它手里持有的描述符，也就是上一章的那些能力。

cbdbf6235ad0.en: The browser is where these walls meet strangers' code every day. <bookmark mark='a'/> A privileged browser process talks to the network and the disk, and each site runs in its own sandboxed renderer. <bookmark mark='b'/> After Spectre, anything in the same address space could be read by speculation, so the wall between sites had to be a process, and in 2018 Chrome turned site isolation on by default on the desktop. <bookmark mark='c'/> Inside a page, WebAssembly, in every major browser since 2017, is a sandbox within a process: every load is checked against its linear memory, and control reaches only validated code. <bookmark mark='d'/> Sixty-four-bit engines reserve the whole range a thirty-two-bit index can reach, plus guard pages, so the bounds check is Part 32's paging, done in hardware.
cbdbf6235ad0.zh: 浏览器，是这些墙每天与陌生人的代码相遇的地方。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个有特权的浏览器进程与网络和磁盘打交道，每个网站都在它自己的沙箱化渲染器里运行。<bookmark mark='b'/>在 Spectre 之后，同一个地址空间里的任何东西，都可能被推测执行读到，所以网站之间的墙必须是一个进程，2018年，Chrome 在桌面端默认打开了站点隔离。<bookmark mark='c'/>在页面内部，WebAssembly，自2017年起存在于每一个主流浏览器中，是一个进程之内的沙箱：每一次加载，都要对照它的线性内存做检查，控制流只能到达经过验证的代码。<bookmark mark='d'/>64位的引擎会把32位下标所能到达的整个范围保留下来，再加上保护页，所以边界检查就是第32部分的分页，由硬件来完成。

18265201677c.en: Every wall so far trusts the kernel. An enclave turns that around. <bookmark mark='a'/> Intel's SGX, from 2015, lets an application seal a region of memory that the processor encrypts and keeps even from the operating system and the hypervisor, and it can attest to a remote party what code is inside. <bookmark mark='b'/> But the operating system still manages the enclave's page tables. In 2015 Xu, Cui and Peinado showed that it can unmap pages and watch which ones the enclave faults on; when a branch depends on a secret, that sequence spells it out. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 2018 Foreshadow used speculative execution to read enclave memory outright. <bookmark mark='d'/> An enclave still shares the core, the caches and the page tables with the adversary it excludes. Isolation is only as good as what is not shared.
18265201677c.zh: 到目前为止，每一堵墙都信任内核。飞地（enclave）把这一点反了过来。<bookmark mark='a'/>Intel 自2015年起的 SGX，让应用程序封存一块内存区域，处理器会把它加密，并且连操作系统和虚拟机管理程序也不让碰，它还可以向远程的一方证明里面是什么代码。<bookmark mark='b'/>但操作系统仍然管理着飞地的页表。2015年，Xu、Cui 和 Peinado 表明，它可以取消页的映射，并观察飞地在哪些页上出错；当一个分支取决于一个秘密时，那串页的序列就把它拼写了出来。<bookmark mark='c'/>2018年，Foreshadow 用推测执行直接读出了飞地的内存。<bookmark mark='d'/>飞地依然与它所排除的对手共享核心、缓存和页表。隔离的好坏，只取决于没有被共享的东西。

f6f6fe1d333b.en: A web page runs code from whoever sent it, so the browser needs a rule about whose data that code may touch. <bookmark mark='a'/> It is the same-origin policy, and an origin is three things: scheme, host and port. <bookmark mark='b'/> A script may read only what comes from its own origin. Change the scheme or the port, or add a subdomain, and it is a stranger. <bookmark mark='c'/> But a page may still send requests to origins it cannot read, and most web attacks live in that gap, or in code that slips inside an origin.
f6f6fe1d333b.zh: 网页会运行发送它的任何人的代码，所以浏览器需要一条规则，规定这些代码可以碰谁的数据。<bookmark mark='a'/>这就是同源策略，而一个源由三样东西组成：协议、主机和端口。<bookmark mark='b'/>脚本只能读来自它自己那个源的东西。改变协议或端口，或者加上一个子域名，它就是陌生人。<bookmark mark='c'/>但页面仍然可以向它读不了的源发送请求，大多数 Web 攻击就存在于这道缝隙里，或者存在于那些溜进某个源内部的代码里。

ccd326410a7c.en: The first way in is to slip inside. <bookmark mark='a'/> A site shows comments through a template, and someone posts a comment that is a script. <bookmark mark='b'/> Pasted in raw, its bytes reach the browser's HTML parser, Part 42's state machine, as markup. <bookmark mark='c'/> Parsing our output finds a live script element, which would run with the site's own authority and read its users' cookies: cross-site scripting. <bookmark mark='d'/> Escape the same bytes and the parser finds only text. <bookmark mark='e'/> The defences stack: escape for the context, a Content Security Policy that refuses inline scripts, and HTTP-only cookies that scripts cannot see.
ccd326410a7c.zh: 第一种进入的办法，是溜进去。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个网站通过模板显示评论，而有人发表的评论是一段脚本。<bookmark mark='b'/>被原样粘贴进去，它的字节就会作为标记，到达浏览器的 HTML 解析器，也就是第42部分的那台状态机。<bookmark mark='c'/>解析我们的输出，会发现一个活动的 script 元素，它会以网站自己的权限运行，并读取用户的 cookie：这就是跨站脚本。<bookmark mark='d'/>把同样的字节转义，解析器就只看到文本。<bookmark mark='e'/>防御是层层叠加的：按上下文转义，一条拒绝内联脚本的内容安全策略（Content Security Policy），以及脚本看不见的 HTTP-only cookie。

96fe3c05681e.en: The second way in uses the gap. <bookmark mark='a'/> You visit an evil page while logged in to your bank, and it submits a hidden form aimed at the bank. <bookmark mark='b'/> Your browser sends the request and, as for every request to the bank, attaches your session cookie. <bookmark mark='c'/> The bank sees a valid session, and obeys. <bookmark mark='d'/> The browser is Chapter six's confused deputy, lending its ambient authority to anyone who names the bank. <bookmark mark='e'/> The fixes are that chapter's too: same-site cookies stay off cross-site requests like this one, and a secret token in each genuine form is a capability the evil page cannot read.
96fe3c05681e.zh: 第二种进入的办法，利用的是那道缝隙。<bookmark mark='a'/>你在登录着银行的时候，访问了一个恶意页面，它提交了一个指向银行的隐藏表单。<bookmark mark='b'/>你的浏览器发出这个请求，并且像对银行的每一个请求那样，附上你的会话 cookie。<bookmark mark='c'/>银行看到一个有效的会话，于是照办。<bookmark mark='d'/>浏览器就是第六章的那个混淆代理，把自己的环境权限借给任何指名银行的人。<bookmark mark='e'/>修复办法也来自那一章：同站 cookie 不随像这样的跨站请求发送，而每个真实表单里的秘密令牌，就是恶意页面读不到的一种能力。

8ce17111904f.en: Now the same confusion on a server, with Part 35's database engine. <bookmark mark='a'/> A lookup builds its query by pasting the user's input into the SQL text. <bookmark mark='b'/> Given two, the parser compares the column id with the literal two, and one row comes back. <bookmark mark='c'/> Given the letters i, d, the parser reads a second column name. Id equals id holds for every row, the filter dissolves, and our engine returns all three secrets. <bookmark mark='d'/> Nothing overflowed and nothing was guessed: the input reached the parser and changed the program's shape. Injection was described publicly in 1998, and is still among the commonest web flaws.
8ce17111904f.zh: 现在是服务器上的同一种混淆，用的是第35部分的数据库引擎。<bookmark mark='a'/>一次查询，通过把用户的输入粘贴进 SQL 文本来构造它的查询语句。<bookmark mark='b'/>输入 2，解析器就把列 id 与字面量 2 比较，返回一行。<bookmark mark='c'/>输入字母 i、d，解析器就读到了第二个列名。id 等于 id，对每一行都成立，过滤条件就消解了，于是我们的引擎返回了全部三个秘密。<bookmark mark='d'/>什么都没有溢出，什么都没有靠猜：输入到达了解析器，并改变了程序的形状。注入在1998年被公开描述，至今仍是最常见的 Web 缺陷之一。

ba58abbc7f13.en: The cure is not to hunt for dangerous characters. It is Part 12's lesson about parsing. <bookmark mark='a'/> Parse the template once, with a hole for each value, so the tree's shape is fixed before any input arrives; then drop values in as finished leaves, never as text. <bookmark mark='b'/> Bound this way, i, d is just a string, and no user has that name. <bookmark mark='c'/> Run the classic login payloads both ways. Pasted in, they reach our parser, which stops on syntax it lacks; a full database would have obeyed. Bound, each is merely a strange username.
ba58abbc7f13.zh: 解药不是去搜寻危险字符。它是第12部分关于解析的那一课。<bookmark mark='a'/>把模板解析一次，给每个值留一个洞，这样在任何输入到达之前，树的形状就已经固定；然后把值作为现成的叶子放进去，绝不作为文本。<bookmark mark='b'/>这样绑定之后，i、d 只是一个字符串，没有哪个用户叫这个名字。<bookmark mark='c'/>把经典的登录攻击载荷用两种方式各跑一遍。粘贴进去的时候，它们到达我们的解析器，解析器会在它不支持的语法上停下；而一个完整的数据库会照办。绑定之后，每一个都只是一个奇怪的用户名。

3e29e4c88231.en: Beneath it all sits Part 30's public-key infrastructure, and it can fail too. <bookmark mark='a'/> Your browser trusts a store of root authorities, and any of them may vouch for any name. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2011 the Dutch authority DigiNotar was broken into, and a certificate for every google dot com address was issued and used to intercept users in Iran. <bookmark mark='c'/> Chrome, which pinned Google's keys, noticed; the browsers removed DigiNotar, and it was bankrupt within the year. <bookmark mark='d'/> The structural fix, Certificate Transparency, from 2013, puts every certificate in public, append-only Merkle logs, so a rogue one cannot hide.
3e29e4c88231.zh: 在这一切的底下，是第30部分的公钥基础设施，而它也可能失效。<bookmark mark='a'/>你的浏览器信任一个根机构的库，而其中任何一个都可以为任何名字担保。<bookmark mark='b'/>2011年，荷兰的机构 DigiNotar 被攻破，一份针对每一个 google 点 com 地址的证书被签发出来，并被用来拦截伊朗的用户。<bookmark mark='c'/>固定了 Google 密钥的 Chrome 注意到了；各个浏览器移除了 DigiNotar，它在当年之内就破产了。<bookmark mark='d'/>结构性的修复，是2013年起的证书透明度（Certificate Transparency），它把每一份证书放进公开的、只能追加的 Merkle 日志里，所以流氓证书藏不住。

aab037c33d67.zh: 第九章：受到攻击的网络。

58909b89f847.en: Every packet carries two addresses, and the network only cares about one of them. <bookmark mark='a'/> Routers forward by the destination, Part 36's longest-prefix match, and nothing on the way checks the source. <bookmark mark='b'/> So an attacker can write someone else's address there. <bookmark mark='c'/> The packet travels as usual, the reflector answers it, and the answer goes to the forged source, a victim who never asked. <bookmark mark='d'/> The fix has been known since 2000, as best current practice thirty-eight: each edge network drops packets whose source is not one of its own. It works only where it is deployed, which is not everywhere.
58909b89f847.zh: 每个数据包都带着两个地址，而网络只关心其中一个。<bookmark mark='a'/>路由器按目的地址转发，也就是第36部分的最长前缀匹配，而沿途没有任何东西检查源地址。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以攻击者可以在那里写上别人的地址。<bookmark mark='c'/>数据包照常传输，反射器回答它，而回答被送到了伪造的源地址，一个从未发出过请求的受害者那里。<bookmark mark='d'/>修复办法自2000年起就已为人所知，即最佳当前实践第38号：每个边缘网络丢弃源地址不属于自己的数据包。它只在部署的地方起作用，而并非到处都部署了。

07ec82edb88d.en: Add a protocol whose answer is bigger than its question, and a forged source becomes a lever. <bookmark mark='a'/> The attacker sends n small requests a second, q bytes each, all claiming to come from the victim. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each reflector answers with r bytes, and every answer lands on the victim. <bookmark mark='c'/> Divide one rate by the other and n cancels: <bookmark mark='d'/> the victim receives A times what the attacker sent, A being the answer's size over the question's. <bookmark mark='e'/> It needs UDP, with no handshake; a TCP connection must first prove its source can receive, Part 37's handshake doing security work.
07ec82edb88d.zh: 加上一个回答比提问更大的协议，伪造的源地址就成了一根杠杆。<bookmark mark='a'/>攻击者每秒发送 n 个小请求，每个 q 字节，全都声称来自受害者。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个反射器用 r 字节来回答，而每一个回答都落到了受害者身上。<bookmark mark='c'/>用一个速率除以另一个速率，n 就消掉了：<bookmark mark='d'/>受害者收到的，是攻击者所发出的 A 倍，A 是回答的大小除以提问的大小。<bookmark mark='e'/>这需要 UDP，没有握手；而一个 TCP 连接必须先证明它的源地址能够接收，第37部分的握手在做安全的工作。

7f54777798a9.en: How big is A? <bookmark mark='a'/> America's computer emergency team published measured factors in 2014: about six for a management protocol, tens for device discovery and for DNS; <bookmark mark='b'/> hundreds for an old diagnostic service and for NTP, the time protocol. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 2018 came memcached, a cache server some had left open to the internet: up to fifty-one thousand. That February GitHub absorbed about one point three five terabits a second of it. <bookmark mark='d'/> One megabit of forged questions becomes fifty-one gigabits of answers. The defences: filter sources, close open reflectors, and absorb the rest at Part 37's anycast edge.
7f54777798a9.zh: A 有多大？<bookmark mark='a'/>美国的计算机应急小组在2014年公布了实测的放大系数：一种管理协议大约是6，设备发现和 DNS 是几十；<bookmark mark='b'/>一种老的诊断服务和 NTP，也就是时间协议，是几百。<bookmark mark='c'/>2018年出现了 memcached，一种有些人让它向互联网敞开的缓存服务器：最高达到51000。那年2月，GitHub 承受了其中大约每秒1.35太比特。<bookmark mark='d'/>1兆比特的伪造提问，变成51吉比特的回答。防御办法：过滤源地址，关闭开放的反射器，并在第37部分的任播边缘吸收其余的流量。

194c3d7204d5.en: Between networks, BGP believes what it is told. <bookmark mark='a'/> On Part 36's internet of a hundred and twenty-five networks, the owner of an address block announces it and everyone routes there. <bookmark mark='b'/> If a stranger announces the same block, the forty-nine networks nearer to it believe the stranger. <bookmark mark='c'/> If it announces a more specific block inside, the longest prefix wins everywhere, and every network sends the traffic the wrong way: what Pakistan Telecom did to YouTube in 2008, by mistake. <bookmark mark='d'/> Signed route origins, the RPKI, repair it network by network: with a quarter of them checking, sixty-one are still fooled.
194c3d7204d5.zh: 在网络之间，BGP 别人说什么就信什么。<bookmark mark='a'/>在第36部分那个有125个网络的互联网上，一个地址块的所有者宣告它，所有网络就都往那里路由。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果一个陌生人宣告同一个地址块，离它更近的49个网络，就会相信这个陌生人。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果它宣告里面一个更具体的地址块，最长前缀就在所有地方胜出，每个网络都把流量送往错误的方向：这就是巴基斯坦电信2008年对 YouTube 做的事，出于失误。<bookmark mark='d'/>有签名的路由起源，也就是 RPKI，一个网络一个网络地修复它：在四分之一的网络做检查的情况下，仍有61个被骗。

560dfa40d03a.en: Part 37 met Kaminsky's attack on DNS. Here is its arithmetic. <bookmark mark='a'/> In each race the attacker sends k forged answers, each guessing the resolver's H-bit number. <bookmark mark='b'/> A fresh random name makes every race a new try, so the expected number of races is one over p: two to the H over k. <bookmark mark='c'/> With only the sixteen-bit query identifier and a hundred forgeries a race, that is about six hundred and fifty-six races, about a minute. <bookmark mark='d'/> The 2008 fix randomised the source port as well: sixteen more bits, about forty-three million races, some fifty days. <bookmark mark='e'/> Randomness only raises the price. Signing the answers, with DNSSEC, removes the guess.
560dfa40d03a.zh: 第37部分见过 Kaminsky 对 DNS 的攻击。这是它的算术。<bookmark mark='a'/>在每一场赛跑中，攻击者发送 k 个伪造的回答，每一个都在猜解析器的那个 H 比特的数。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个新的随机名字，让每场赛跑都成为一次新的尝试，所以赛跑的期望次数是 p 分之一：2 的 H 次方除以 k。<bookmark mark='c'/>只有16比特的查询标识符，每场赛跑伪造100个，就是大约656场赛跑，大约一分钟。<bookmark mark='d'/>2008年的修复把源端口也随机化了：多出16比特，大约4300万场赛跑，约50天。<bookmark mark='e'/>随机性只是抬高了价格。用 DNSSEC 给回答签名，则消除了这个猜测。

1f48af3810b8.en: So what should a program believe about the network? Nothing. <bookmark mark='a'/> Between you and a server sit links, providers, resolvers and transit networks, and any of them may read, drop, delay or forge. <bookmark mark='b'/> Part 36's end-to-end argument says to do the important things at the ends, and TLS does: keys agreed between the two ends, with Part 30's mathematics, guard what is said, that it arrives unchanged, and who answered, as long as the certificates hold. <bookmark mark='c'/> What no encryption guards is whether the packets arrive at all, and who is talking to whom. Availability is bought with capacity and filtering, not with keys.
1f48af3810b8.zh: 那么，一个程序应该相信网络的什么？什么都不信。<bookmark mark='a'/>在你和一台服务器之间，隔着链路、服务提供商、解析器和中转网络，其中任何一个都可能读取、丢弃、延迟或伪造。<bookmark mark='b'/>第36部分的端到端论证说，要把重要的事情放在两端去做，TLS 正是这样做的：两端之间用第30部分的数学商定的密钥，守护所说的内容、它到达时是否未被更改，以及是谁作了回答，只要证书可靠。<bookmark mark='c'/>任何加密都守护不了的，是数据包到底到不到得了，以及谁在和谁说话。可用性是用容量和过滤换来的，而不是用密钥。

1e8a5b36feb7.en: A program trusts far more than its compiler. <bookmark mark='a'/> It names three dependencies; they name six more; those name twelve, each written by a stranger and running with your program's authority. <bookmark mark='b'/> If each is clean with probability one minus p, independently, all n are clean with probability one minus p to the n. <bookmark mark='c'/> Take logarithms; <bookmark mark='d'/> for small p, the log of one minus p is about minus p, <bookmark mark='e'/> so the chance that nothing is bad is about e to the minus n p. <bookmark mark='f'/> A thousand packages, one bad in ten thousand: a one in ten chance of trouble, set by the least careful stranger.
1e8a5b36feb7.zh: 一个程序所信任的，远远不止它的编译器。<bookmark mark='a'/>它点名了3个依赖；这些依赖又点名了6个；那6个再点名12个，每一个都出自陌生人之手，并以你的程序的权限运行。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果每一个独立地以 1 减 p 的概率是干净的，那么全部 n 个都干净的概率，就是 1 减 p 的 n 次方。<bookmark mark='c'/>取对数；<bookmark mark='d'/>当 p 很小时，1 减 p 的对数约等于负 p，<bookmark mark='e'/>所以什么都没有坏的概率，大约是 e 的负 np 次方。<bookmark mark='f'/>1000个包，万分之一是坏的：出问题的概率是十分之一，这是由最不小心的那个陌生人决定的。

9ced122ea9b2.en: In 2021 Alex Birsan turned a resolver's own rules against it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Companies keep internal packages in a private registry, under names that leak in public code. <bookmark mark='b'/> Publish the same name on the public registry with a higher version, <bookmark mark='c'/> and an installer that looks in both takes the highest, wherever it lives; the stranger's install script runs inside the company. He reached dozens of companies, and reported it to them. <bookmark mark='d'/> The fixes are names and hashes: a namespace you own, one registry per name, and every package pinned by its content hash, Part 41's lockfile.
9ced122ea9b2.zh: 2021年，Alex Birsan 把解析器自己的规则变成了对付它自己的武器。<bookmark mark='a'/>公司把内部的包放在一个私有注册表里，用的名字会在公开的代码里泄露出去。<bookmark mark='b'/>在公共注册表上，用更高的版本号发布同一个名字，<bookmark mark='c'/>那么一个两处都会查找的安装程序，就会选最高的那个，不管它在哪里；陌生人的安装脚本就在公司内部运行了起来。他触达了几十家公司，并向它们报告了此事。<bookmark mark='d'/>修复办法是名字和哈希：一个你所拥有的命名空间，每个名字只对应一个注册表，并且每个包都用它的内容哈希固定下来，也就是第41部分的锁文件。

0fa44d763470.en: The build is another way in. <bookmark mark='a'/> SolarWinds sells Orion, software that monitors networks and so is trusted with them. <bookmark mark='b'/> Attackers inside its build environment made the build insert a backdoor as it ran, so the source repository stayed clean, <bookmark mark='c'/> and every binary was then signed with the company's own key and shipped as a routine update. <bookmark mark='d'/> When it was disclosed in December 2020, found by FireEye while investigating a breach of its own, SolarWinds put the number of customers who had installed it at fewer than eighteen thousand. <bookmark mark='e'/> The signature was genuine. It said who built the binary, not what it was built from.
0fa44d763470.zh: 构建，是另一条进入的路。<bookmark mark='a'/>SolarWinds 出售 Orion，这是一款监控网络的软件，因此被信任可以接触这些网络。<bookmark mark='b'/>处于它构建环境内部的攻击者，让构建在运行时插入了一个后门，所以源代码仓库一直是干净的，<bookmark mark='c'/>随后每个二进制文件都用公司自己的密钥签了名，作为例行更新发布出去。<bookmark mark='d'/>2020年12月披露这件事时，是 FireEye 在调查它自己遭到的一次攻破时发现的，SolarWinds 给出的安装了它的客户数量是不到18000家。<bookmark mark='e'/>签名是真的。它说明的是谁构建了这个二进制文件，而不是它由什么构建而成。

691823f9f736.en: And sometimes the supplier is the attacker. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2021 a newcomer began sending patches to xz-utils, a compression library inside almost every Linux system, maintained by one volunteer. <bookmark mark='b'/> Other accounts pressed him to share the work, and the newcomer became a co-maintainer. <bookmark mark='c'/> In early 2024 two releases carried a backdoor. <bookmark mark='d'/> It was not in the repository that reviewers read, but in the release archives distributions build from, where a changed build script unpacked code hidden in binary test files into the library. <bookmark mark='e'/> Where OpenSSH's server loads that library through systemd, it intercepted the check of a client's key, so only the attacker's key could open it.
691823f9f736.zh: 而有时，供应商就是攻击者。<bookmark mark='a'/>2021年，一个新人开始向 xz-utils 提交补丁，那是一个压缩库，几乎存在于每一个 Linux 系统里，由一位志愿者维护。<bookmark mark='b'/>另一些账号催促他把工作分出去，于是这个新人成了共同维护者。<bookmark mark='c'/>2024年初，有两个发布版本带着一个后门。<bookmark mark='d'/>它不在审阅者阅读的仓库里，而在各发行版用来构建的发布归档里，在那里，一份被修改过的构建脚本，把藏在二进制测试文件里的代码解包进了这个库。<bookmark mark='e'/>在 OpenSSH 的服务器通过 systemd 加载这个库的地方，它拦截了对客户端密钥的检查，所以只有攻击者的密钥才能打开它。

a3fd7bdc16db.en: It was found by accident. <bookmark mark='a'/> On the twenty-ninth of March 2024, Andres Freund, a PostgreSQL developer benchmarking on Debian's unstable branch, noticed the SSH server using unexpected processor time, logins about half a second slower, and a memory checker complaining. <bookmark mark='b'/> He traced it to the compression library and reported it publicly. <bookmark mark='c'/> The stable releases of the major distributions had not yet shipped it. Two years of patient preparation were undone by half a second, noticed by one engineer: Chapter four's side channel, working for once for the defence.
a3fd7bdc16db.zh: 它是意外被发现的。<bookmark mark='a'/>2024年3月29日，Andres Freund，一位在 Debian 的不稳定分支上做基准测试的 PostgreSQL 开发者，注意到 SSH 服务器占用了意料之外的处理器时间，登录大约慢了半秒，还有一个内存检查器在报错。<bookmark mark='b'/>他追查到了那个压缩库，并公开报告了此事。<bookmark mark='c'/>主要发行版的稳定版本还没有发布它。两年耐心的准备，被半秒钟毁掉了，而发现这半秒的是一位工程师：这是第四章的侧信道，难得一次地为防御方服务。

2ac470577a81.en: The defences make each link checkable. <bookmark mark='a'/> A commit is named by its hash; the build records signed provenance, which source and which builder; the artifact's hash is pinned in a lockfile; the deployer checks both. <bookmark mark='b'/> The SLSA framework, from 2021, grades this evidence; a bill of materials lists every component, so that when the next backdoor is found, everyone can tell at once whether they run it. <bookmark mark='c'/> And reproducible builds let anyone rebuild from source and compare bytes, which is where the next chapter begins. <bookmark mark='d'/> None of it checks that the source is honest. That still takes people reading it.
2ac470577a81.zh: 这些防御让每一环都可以检查。<bookmark mark='a'/>一次提交由它的哈希命名；构建记录下有签名的来源证明，包括哪份源代码、哪个构建者；制品的哈希被固定在一个锁文件里；部署者检查这两者。<bookmark mark='b'/>SLSA 框架，起于2021年，给这份证据评级；软件物料清单列出每一个组件，这样当下一个后门被发现时，每个人都能立刻知道自己是否在运行它。<bookmark mark='c'/>而可重现构建，让任何人都能从源代码重新构建并逐字节比较，下一章就从这里开始。<bookmark mark='d'/>这一切都没有检查源代码是否诚实。那仍然需要人去阅读它。

0f71e7ea1437.en: Chapter eleven. Reflections on trusting trust.
0f71e7ea1437.zh: 第十一章：关于对信任的信任的反思。

dbc90b6b4b2e.en: Ken Thompson's lecture, published in 1984, builds its attack in three stages, and we will build each. <bookmark mark='a'/> A compiler is a program that turns source text into bytes; here the language is Python and a binary is its compiled code, but nothing else matters. <bookmark mark='b'/> The login program accepts one password. <bookmark mark='c'/> Compile the compiler's source and you get a compiler binary of four hundred and ninety-nine bytes. <bookmark mark='d'/> Run that binary on login's source and you get a login binary. A compiler can compile any program, including its own source: everything Thompson needs. <bookmark mark='e'/> The marked empty slot is only there to make our demonstration easy to read.
dbc90b6b4b2e.zh: 肯·汤普森那篇1984年发表的演讲，分三个阶段构建它的攻击，我们会把每一个都搭出来。<bookmark mark='a'/>编译器是一个把源文本变成字节的程序；这里的语言是 Python，二进制文件就是它编译出来的代码，但别的都无关紧要。<bookmark mark='b'/>login 程序只接受一个密码。<bookmark mark='c'/>编译这个编译器的源代码，你得到一个499字节的编译器二进制文件。<bookmark mark='d'/>用这个二进制文件去编译 login 的源代码，你得到一个 login 二进制文件。编译器可以编译任何程序，包括它自己的源代码：汤普森所需要的一切。<bookmark mark='e'/>那个被标出来的空槽，只是为了让我们的演示容易看懂。

04f605550905.en: Stage one is an ordinary backdoor. <bookmark mark='a'/> Add one line to login: if the password is a magic word, let them in. <bookmark mark='b'/> Compiled, the honest login lets in the right password and refuses everything else. The backdoored one also lets in the magic word, and still refuses a wrong guess, so nobody using it notices anything. <bookmark mark='c'/> But the line is in login's source, and anyone who reads the source will see it. The attack must leave the source.
04f605550905.zh: 第一阶段是一个普通的后门。<bookmark mark='a'/>给 login 加一行：如果密码是一个魔法词，就放他们进去。<bookmark mark='b'/>编译之后，诚实的 login 放行正确的密码，拒绝其他一切。带后门的那个也放行魔法词，并且仍然拒绝错误的猜测，所以使用它的人什么也察觉不到。<bookmark mark='c'/>但这一行就在 login 的源代码里，任何阅读源代码的人都会看到。攻击必须离开源代码。

9799602d8521.en: Stage two moves the line out of login and into the compiler. <bookmark mark='a'/> The compiler looks at what it is compiling. If it recognises login, it quietly adds the backdoor before compiling. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now login's source is honest, and anyone may audit it. <bookmark mark='c'/> But compiled by this compiler, login comes out two hundred and seventy-nine bytes long instead of two hundred and thirty-six, with the magic word inside. <bookmark mark='d'/> We have only moved the problem: the trick is now in the compiler's source, and compilers have readers too.
9799602d8521.zh: 第二阶段把这一行从 login 里移出来，放进编译器。<bookmark mark='a'/>编译器会看它正在编译的是什么。如果它认出了 login，就在编译之前悄悄加上后门。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在 login 的源代码是诚实的，任何人都可以审计它。<bookmark mark='c'/>但经过这个编译器编译，login 出来的长度是279字节，而不是236字节，里面带着魔法词。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们只是把问题挪了个地方：这个花招现在在编译器的源代码里，而编译器也有读者。

ae71560666d5.en: Stage three is the clever one, and it is Part 25's quine. <bookmark mark='a'/> Teach the compiler a second trick: when it compiles a compiler, insert the trojan itself into the output. For that the trojan must know its own text. <bookmark mark='b'/> Write it as a template T with one hole, and form the block B by pasting T into its own hole. <bookmark mark='c'/> Inside B, the variable q holds the template. <bookmark mark='d'/> So q pasted into q is T pasted into T, <bookmark mark='e'/> which is B. The trojan can write out an exact copy of itself, exactly as a quine prints its own source. <bookmark mark='f'/> And that means the compiler's source no longer needs to contain it.
ae71560666d5.zh: 第三阶段是最巧妙的，它就是第25部分的自打印程序（quine）。<bookmark mark='a'/>教编译器第二个花招：当它编译一个编译器时，把木马本身插进输出里。为此，木马必须知道自己的文本。<bookmark mark='b'/>把它写成一个带一个洞的模板 T，再把 T 粘贴进它自己的那个洞，形成块 B。<bookmark mark='c'/>在 B 的内部，变量 q 保存着模板。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以把 q 粘贴进 q，就是把 T 粘贴进 T，<bookmark mark='e'/>也就是 B。木马可以写出一份与自己一模一样的副本，就像自打印程序打印出它自己的源代码一样。<bookmark mark='f'/>而这意味着，编译器的源代码不再需要包含它了。

7d9209d1392c.en: Now delete every trace of the trojan from the compiler's source. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take the trojaned binary and give it the clean source to compile. <bookmark mark='b'/> It recognises a compiler, and inserts itself. The binary it produces has the same eleven hundred and nineteen bytes and the same hash: <bookmark mark='c'/> bit for bit the binary we started with. <bookmark mark='d'/> So the loop is a fixed point. Rebuild the compiler from clean source as often as you like, and every generation is the trojan again. <bookmark mark='e'/> And each of them, compiling the honest login, still lets in the magic word.
7d9209d1392c.zh: 现在把木马的每一点痕迹，都从编译器的源代码里删掉。<bookmark mark='a'/>拿起被植入木马的二进制文件，让它去编译那份干净的源代码。<bookmark mark='b'/>它认出这是一个编译器，并把自己插进去。它产生的二进制文件，有同样的1119字节，和同样的哈希：<bookmark mark='c'/>与我们开始时的那个二进制文件逐位相同。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以这个循环是一个不动点。你想从干净的源代码重新构建多少次编译器都行，每一代又都是木马。<bookmark mark='e'/>而它们中的每一个，在编译诚实的 login 时，仍然放行魔法词。

10098f468817.en: That is the whole attack. <bookmark mark='a'/> Search every source file for the magic password and you will not find it. <bookmark mark='b'/> Yet the compiler you run carries the trojan, and the login you run lets in the magic word. <bookmark mark='c'/> Thompson's moral was blunt: no amount of source-level verification or scrutiny will protect you from using untrusted code. <bookmark mark='d'/> And he noted that he could have picked on any program that handles programs, an assembler, a loader, even hardware microcode, and that the lower the level, the harder such a bug is to detect. He credited the idea to an Air Force review of Multics in the 1970s. It looks hopeless. The next chapter shows that it is not.
10098f468817.zh: 这就是整个攻击。<bookmark mark='a'/>在每一个源文件里搜索那个魔法密码，你找不到它。<bookmark mark='b'/>然而你所运行的编译器带着木马，你所运行的 login 放行魔法词。<bookmark mark='c'/>汤普森的寓意很直白：再多的源代码层面的验证或审查，也不能保护你不去使用不可信的代码。<bookmark mark='d'/>他还指出，他本可以挑任何处理程序的程序下手，汇编器、装入程序，甚至硬件的微码，而且层次越低，这样的错误就越难发现。他把这个想法归功于1970年代空军对 Multics 的一次评审。看起来毫无希望。下一章表明，并非如此。

fb4a6ad9b4c9.zh: 第十二章：抓住特洛伊木马。

7d43a7ff9c45.en: In 2005 David Wheeler published the answer, and in 2009 his thesis proved it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Keep the binary you suspect, A, and the compiler's source, c, which you can read. <bookmark mark='b'/> Add a second compiler, T, written independently. It may be slow, or old, or imperfect; it need not be trusted in general. <bookmark mark='c'/> Ours is a reference compiler that never inspects what it compiles, so it cannot carry a trojan that recognises compilers. <bookmark mark='d'/> The one assumption is that A and T are not trojaned in the same way: the trojan would have to be in both.
7d43a7ff9c45.zh: 2005年，David Wheeler 发表了答案，2009年，他的论文证明了它。<bookmark mark='a'/>保留你怀疑的那个二进制文件 A，以及编译器的源代码 c，它你是可以阅读的。<bookmark mark='b'/>再加上第二个编译器 T，独立写成。它可以很慢，或者很老，或者并不完美；它不需要在一般意义上被信任。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们的是一个参考编译器，它从不检查它所编译的是什么，所以它不可能带有一个能认出编译器的木马。<bookmark mark='d'/>唯一的假设是，A 和 T 没有以同样的方式被植入木马：木马得同时存在于两者之中。

8e12ae7b5b47.en: The procedure has two stages. <bookmark mark='a'/> Stage one: compile the source c with the independent compiler, giving a new compiler binary X. Its bytes will differ from A's, because different compilers write different code. <bookmark mark='b'/> Stage two: compile c again, this time with X, giving Z. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now suppose A really was compiled from c. Then X and A were built from the same source and do the same thing, so they give the same output on the same input: Z equals A of c. <bookmark mark='d'/> And a compiler compiling its own source reproduces itself, so A of c is A. <bookmark mark='e'/> The test is to compare Z with A, bit for bit.
8e12ae7b5b47.zh: 这个过程分两个阶段。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一阶段：用那个独立的编译器编译源代码 c，得到一个新的编译器二进制文件 X。它的字节会与 A 的不同，因为不同的编译器写出的代码不同。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二阶段：再编译一次 c，这一次用 X，得到 Z。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在假设 A 确实是由 c 编译出来的。那么 X 和 A 是由同一份源代码构建的，行为相同，所以对相同的输入给出相同的输出：Z 等于 A 作用于 c 的结果。<bookmark mark='d'/>而一个编译器编译它自己的源代码，会复现它自己，所以 A 作用于 c 的结果就是 A。<bookmark mark='e'/>检验就是把 Z 和 A 逐位比较。

606ad4ea2ce4.en: First, run it on an honest compiler. <bookmark mark='a'/> In stage one, the suspect produces four hundred and ninety-nine bytes, the independent compiler four hundred and ninety-eight, with different hashes. That is expected: two compilers, two ways of writing the same program. <bookmark mark='b'/> In stage two, both of those binaries compile the same source, <bookmark mark='c'/> and the results are identical, bit for bit, and identical to A. <bookmark mark='d'/> The verdict: A really is what its source says.
606ad4ea2ce4.zh: 首先，在一个诚实的编译器上运行它。<bookmark mark='a'/>在第一阶段，被怀疑的那个产生499字节，独立的编译器产生498字节，哈希不同。这是预料之中的：两个编译器，是写同一个程序的两种方式。<bookmark mark='b'/>在第二阶段，这两个二进制文件都去编译同一份源代码，<bookmark mark='c'/>结果逐位相同，并且与 A 相同。<bookmark mark='d'/>结论：A 确实就是它的源代码所说的那样。

90243381bb7c.en: Now the binary from the last chapter. <bookmark mark='a'/> Stage one: the suspect, compiling the clean source, inserts its trojan, and gives eleven hundred and nineteen bytes; the independent compiler gives an honest four hundred and ninety-eight. <bookmark mark='b'/> Stage two: the suspect's lineage reproduces the trojan again, while X, an honest compiler built by an honest compiler, produces the honest binary. <bookmark mark='c'/> They differ. <bookmark mark='d'/> Trojan detected. The trojan could fool any amount of reading, but it cannot be in a compiler it never touched.
90243381bb7c.zh: 现在是上一章的那个二进制文件。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一阶段：被怀疑的那个在编译干净的源代码时，插入它的木马，给出1119字节；独立的编译器给出诚实的498字节。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二阶段：被怀疑的这一系又一次复现出木马，而 X，一个由诚实的编译器构建的诚实的编译器，产生出诚实的二进制文件。<bookmark mark='c'/>它们不同。<bookmark mark='d'/>木马被发现了。木马可以骗过任意多的阅读，但它不可能存在于一个它从未碰过的编译器里。

52700b041647.en: Comparing bit for bit assumes a build gives the same bits every time, and real builds often do not. <bookmark mark='a'/> Our toy build stamps the time and the directory into its header, so Alice and Bob, building the same source, get different hashes, and a comparison proves nothing. <bookmark mark='b'/> Fix the time and the path, and the two builds are identical. <bookmark mark='c'/> Since 2013 the Tor and Debian projects have led the work of making real builds reproducible: fixed timestamps, sorted file lists, no build paths. A reproducible build lets anyone rebuild a release and check it, which also checks that a release matches the public source, the very gap xz exploited.
52700b041647.zh: 逐位比较，是假定一次构建每次给出同样的比特，而真实的构建往往并非如此。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们的玩具构建会把时间和目录戳进它的头部，所以 Alice 和 Bob 构建同一份源代码，得到不同的哈希，比较就什么也证明不了。<bookmark mark='b'/>把时间和路径固定下来，这两次构建就相同了。<bookmark mark='c'/>自2013年起，Tor 和 Debian 项目带头推动让真实的构建可重现：固定的时间戳，排好序的文件列表，没有构建路径。可重现构建让任何人都能重新构建一个发布版并检查它，这也就检查了发布版是否与公开的源代码一致，而这正是 xz 所利用的那道缺口。

2e50ad2aa6fa.en: Where does the trusted compiler come from? <bookmark mark='a'/> The bootstrapping projects answer by growing one from a seed: a program of a few hundred bytes, written in hexadecimal, small enough for a person to read. It builds a tiny assembler, which builds a minimal C compiler, then a small real one, then an early GCC, and finally the modern toolchain. GNU Guix announced such a full-source bootstrap in 2023. <bookmark mark='b'/> Diverse double-compiling then proves that a binary is what its source says. It assumes that the second compiler is not trojaned the same way, so use several of different origins. <bookmark mark='c'/> And it cannot prove the source honest: someone must still read it.
2e50ad2aa6fa.zh: 那个可信的编译器从哪里来？<bookmark mark='a'/>自举项目的回答，是从一颗种子把它长出来：一个只有几百字节的程序，用十六进制写成，小到一个人可以读完。它构建一个很小的汇编器，汇编器构建一个最小的 C 编译器，然后是一个小的真正的编译器，再然后是一个早期的 GCC，最后是现代的工具链。GNU Guix 在2023年宣布了这样一次全源码自举。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后，多样化双重编译证明一个二进制文件就是它的源代码所说的那样。它假定第二个编译器没有以同样的方式被植入木马，所以要使用几个不同来源的。<bookmark mark='c'/>而且它无法证明源代码是诚实的：仍然得有人去读它。

697b4786ebe9.en: Chapter thirteen. The tower, end to end.
697b4786ebe9.zh: 第十三章：整座塔，从头到尾。

f66c9e483c1a.en: Follow the Job one last time, from the bottom. <bookmark mark='a'/> A line of Python counts the words of thirty novels, about twenty-five million bytes. Beneath it is a NAND gate made of two switches, then an adder and a register, then Pebble, the computer of Part 6, made fast by pipelines, caches and cores. <bookmark mark='b'/> On it run machine code, a compiler, a runtime, a hash table, and PebbleOS with its traps and pages, a file system and a database. <bookmark mark='c'/> Above them, packets and TCP, Raft and MapReduce, and services on a cluster in the cloud, and at the very top the Job. Every one of these was built in this series, from the one below it, and each one trusts the one below to keep its promise.
f66c9e483c1a.zh: 最后一次，从最底层开始跟随那项任务。<bookmark mark='a'/>一行 Python 数出30本小说的词，大约2500万字节。在它的下面，是一个由两个开关构成的与非门，然后是一个加法器和一个寄存器，然后是 Pebble，也就是第6部分的计算机，靠流水线、缓存和多个核心变快。<bookmark mark='b'/>在它上面运行着机器码、一个编译器、一个运行时、一个哈希表，以及带着陷阱和页的 PebbleOS，一个文件系统和一个数据库。<bookmark mark='c'/>再往上，是数据包和 TCP，Raft 和 MapReduce，以及云上一个集群里的服务，而在最顶端，是那项任务。这当中的每一样，都是在这个系列里，由它下面的那一层搭起来的，而每一层都相信它下面的那一层会信守承诺。

e41c40737a40.en: Now ask each layer what it trusts, and how this series earned it. <bookmark mark='a'/> The switch trusts physics to be on or off; Shannon's algebra made switches into logic, and Part 5's metastability showed where that fails. <bookmark mark='b'/> Gates trust their truth tables, which we checked exhaustively. <bookmark mark='c'/> Arithmetic trusts its adders, checked against arithmetic itself. <bookmark mark='d'/> The instruction set trusts the gates, and the gate-level machine agreed with the emulator on random programs. <bookmark mark='e'/> And every faster core gave Part 6's answers, which is all the architecture promised. It never promised anything about time, and Spectre lives there.
e41c40737a40.zh: 现在问问每一层，它信任什么，以及这个系列是怎样赢得这份信任的。<bookmark mark='a'/>开关信任物理让它非开即关；香农的代数把开关变成了逻辑，而第5部分的亚稳态显示了它在哪里失效。<bookmark mark='b'/>门信任它们的真值表，我们对真值表做过穷举检查。<bookmark mark='c'/>算术信任它的加法器，加法器是拿算术本身来检查的。<bookmark mark='d'/>指令集信任门，而门级的机器在随机程序上与模拟器一致。<bookmark mark='e'/>每一个更快的核心，给出的都是第6部分的答案，而这就是体系结构所承诺的全部。它从未对时间作过任何承诺，而 Spectre 就住在那里。

549b56c29128.en: <bookmark mark='a'/> Machine code trusts that a call returns where it came from; Chapter 2 broke that, and canaries, non-executable memory and randomised layouts defend it. <bookmark mark='b'/> Languages trust the compiler to keep the meaning: we fuzzed ours differentially without a mismatch, proved rewrite rules with z3, and, in this part, checked a compiler against an independent one. <bookmark mark='c'/> Algorithms rest on invariants and proofs, then measurement. <bookmark mark='d'/> The kernel's isolation rests on the memory unit checking every access. <bookmark mark='e'/> And storage promises that a committed write survives a crash, which we tested by crashing it.
549b56c29128.zh: <bookmark mark='a'/>机器码相信一次调用会返回到它来的地方；第2章打破了这一点，而金丝雀、不可执行的内存和随机化的布局为它设防。<bookmark mark='b'/>语言相信编译器会保持含义：我们对自己的编译器做了差分模糊测试，没有发现不一致，用 z3 证明了改写规则，而在这一部分里，还拿一个编译器与一个独立的编译器做了对照检查。<bookmark mark='c'/>算法建立在不变量和证明之上，然后是测量。<bookmark mark='d'/>内核的隔离，建立在内存单元检查每一次访问之上。<bookmark mark='e'/>而存储承诺，已提交的写入能熬过一次崩溃，我们靠让它崩溃来测试了这一点。

e9cbc95de402.en: <bookmark mark='a'/> The network promises bytes in order, and TCP kept that promise under loss and reordering; but who sent the bytes needs the keys of Part 30. <bookmark mark='b'/> Replicas trust Raft to agree, which we checked by injecting failures. <bookmark mark='c'/> Services trust that a retry takes effect once, which idempotency keys made true. <bookmark mark='d'/> And the application at the top earns nothing of its own. It inherits every reason below it, and every leak.
e9cbc95de402.zh: <bookmark mark='a'/>网络承诺字节按顺序到达，而 TCP 在丢包和乱序的情况下信守了这个承诺；但是谁发送了这些字节，则需要第30部分的密钥。<bookmark mark='b'/>副本信任 Raft 会达成一致，我们靠注入故障检查了这一点。<bookmark mark='c'/>服务相信一次重试只会生效一次，幂等键使这一点成真。<bookmark mark='d'/>而位于顶端的应用，自己什么也没有赢得。它继承了它下面的每一条理由，也继承了每一处泄漏。

a66ec1fd48d5.en: Put the reasons side by side, and there are only a few kinds. <bookmark mark='a'/> Proof, for the mathematics and the algorithms. Exhaustive checks, for the gates. Agreement with an independent reference, for the processor and the compiler, the same idea as Wheeler's. Injected failures, for storage, networks and replicas. And hardware that checks every access. <bookmark mark='b'/> The leaks of this part are the places where a layer relied on a promise nobody had checked: that memory cells are independent, that speculation leaves no trace, that a binary matches its source, that a route announcement is honest. Each one crosses the boundary that was supposed to hide it.
a66ec1fd48d5.zh: 把这些理由并排放在一起，只有寥寥几种。<bookmark mark='a'/>证明，用于数学和算法。穷举检查，用于门。与独立参考的一致，用于处理器和编译器，这与 Wheeler 的想法相同。注入故障，用于存储、网络和副本。还有对每一次访问都做检查的硬件。<bookmark mark='b'/>这一部分的那些泄漏，是某一层依赖了一个无人检查过的承诺的地方：内存单元是相互独立的，推测执行不留痕迹，二进制文件与它的源代码相符，路由通告是诚实的。每一处，都越过了本应把它藏起来的边界。

af8521df5f96.en: So here is the tower, lit from end to end. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every layer hides the one below it, and trusts it. <bookmark mark='b'/> Where that trust was earned, by a proof, a check, an independent reference, an injected fault or a key, the layer held. <bookmark mark='c'/> Where it was only assumed, this part found an attack. That is what trusting trust means in the end: not faith in any one layer, but a reason for each.
af8521df5f96.zh: 于是，这就是整座塔，从头到尾被点亮。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一层都把它下面的一层藏起来，并信任它。<bookmark mark='b'/>凡是这份信任是靠一个证明、一次检查、一个独立的参考、一次注入的故障或一把密钥赢得的地方，这一层就守住了。<bookmark mark='c'/>凡是它只是被假定的地方，这一部分就发现了一次攻击。这就是对信任的信任归根结底的含义：不是对任何某一层的信仰，而是对每一层都有一个理由。

4feb462359b2.en: Chapter fourteen, the frontier. What did this series meet that nobody knows?
4feb462359b2.zh: 第十四章，前沿。这个系列遇到了哪些没有人知道答案的问题？

9c10773ccdfa.en: Along the way this series met questions that nobody can answer. <bookmark mark='a'/> Whether P equals NP, and whether one-way functions, and with them all of modern cryptography, exist at all. How fast matrices can be multiplied. The sixth Busy Beaver number, now that the fifth was finally proved in 2024. Whether splay trees are optimal. The unique games conjecture. Whether randomness ever really helps. Why we cannot prove that any explicit function needs many gates. <bookmark mark='b'/> And the practical ones: a memory model for C, quantum computers that do something useful, and verified software at the scale people actually build. Part 61 returns to each of these, as research.
9c10773ccdfa.zh: 一路上，这个系列遇到了一些没有人能回答的问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>P 是否等于 NP，以及单向函数，连同全部的现代密码学，到底是否存在。矩阵乘法能有多快。第6个忙碌海狸数，现在第5个终于在2024年被证明了。伸展树是否最优。唯一博弈猜想。随机性到底有没有真正的帮助。为什么我们无法证明任何一个显式的函数需要很多的门。<bookmark mark='b'/>还有实际的问题：C 的内存模型，能做些有用事情的量子计算机，以及人们实际建造的规模上的经过验证的软件。第61部分会把这每一个都作为研究回过头来讨论。

fb15921a6072.en: Three frontiers of trust in particular. <bookmark mark='a'/> Memory safety at scale: rewriting or hardening billions of lines of C and C++, capabilities built into hardware, and proofs about the unsafe corners of Rust. <bookmark mark='b'/> Speculation: processors that leak nothing through timing, at a cost people will accept, and precise contracts between hardware and software about what may leak. <bookmark mark='c'/> And bootstrapping: building a whole modern toolchain up from a seed program of a few hundred bytes that a person can read, so that Thompson's attack has nowhere to hide. <bookmark mark='d'/> Each turns an informal promise, that a layer hides what is below it, into something that can be checked.
fb15921a6072.zh: 尤其是信任方面的三个前沿。<bookmark mark='a'/>大规模的内存安全：重写或加固数十亿行 C 和 C++，内置于硬件的能力，以及关于 Rust 中 unsafe 角落的证明。<bookmark mark='b'/>推测执行：不通过时间泄漏任何东西的处理器，代价是人们能够接受的，以及硬件与软件之间关于什么可以泄漏的精确契约。<bookmark mark='c'/>还有自举：从一个只有几百字节、人可以阅读的种子程序出发，把一整套现代的工具链搭起来，让汤普森的攻击无处藏身。<bookmark mark='d'/>每一个，都把一个非正式的承诺，也就是一层会把它下面的东西隐藏起来，变成可以检查的东西。
